title: Free AI poster and invitation maker, laid out for you · {name}
description: Give the facts of your event and get an invitation, a poster or a post laid out three ways: pick one, change anything by hand, then print or send it. Free.
h1: Give the facts, and get a design ready to print or post.
acts: and get a design ready to print or post.
lede: An invitation, a poster, a flyer, a menu, a post: tell {name} what it must say. It lays your words out three ways, in colours and type that go together, and opens the first beside your request. Pick a take, move anything, retype any word, then print it or send it as a picture.
cta: Try it with a sample post
try.ask: Make a square post to announce the open day of my pottery studio, Atelier Terre, in Lyon, on 14 June from 2 pm to 6 pm. Come and try the wheel: tea, cake and clay for everyone. It is free, and nobody needs to book.
pane.ask: A post to announce the open day of my pottery studio, on 14 June.
pane.title: A design made in {name}, live
pane.try: This is the design itself. Pick another take in the row above it, double-click any words to change them, or drag a part to move it. A dot marks what needs a look before printing: here, the address to fill in.
pane.asked: In {name}, this points the AI at that part: say what to change, and its change waits for you to accept or reject.
made.name: Open day post
made.occasion: A pottery studio’s open day, warm and friendly
made.title: Open day
made.words: Come and try the wheel. Tea, cake and clay for everyone.
replay.title: One design, step by step.
replay.why: The studio’s post, from the facts to the picture it publishes: what {name} read, what it laid out, and what you finish by hand.
replay.reads: Your request: an open day, its date and hours, what happens, that it is free
What it lacks: the studio’s address, left as a gap in square brackets
replay.works: Gave each fact its role: the big words, the date, the place, who it is from, the small print
Laid them out three ways from its own layouts, in colours and type that go together
Marked what needs a look before printing: the address to fill in
replay.got: The post, open beside your request, with other takes in a row above it. Every part moves, resizes and retypes, by hand or with the keyboard.
replay.made: Its picture, sized for a post, ready to publish, or again for a story. Or a page to print, and the design’s own file, which opens anywhere.
asks.title: Then ask your own
asks.items: A poster for the school fair on 28 June, with its programme.
A menu for Friday’s dinner: three starters, three mains, two desserts.
A square post announcing our new opening hours.
Make the title larger, and the colours warmer.
io.title: What goes in. What comes out.
io.why: Say what it is for and give its facts, as you would to a friend. What is missing is left as a gap for you to fill.
io.ins: What, when, where and who it is from, in your own words
Dropped on the design, it fills its frame
From your design system, placed in its corner
A design for each row: badges, place cards, certificates
io.outs: Three takes to pick from, every part yours to move and retype
Or to save as PDF, two A5s or four A6s to a sheet
As it is, or sized for a post or a story
An SVG that opens anywhere, and in {name} again
exact.title: Laid out by rules, not by chance.
exact.why: An AI that draws a poster as one picture misspells your words, and can’t be corrected. {name} asks the AI for the facts only, and lays them out itself: real words, real shapes, all of them yours to change.
exact.cards: The title, the date and the place are text, not pixels: exactly as you gave them, and yours to retype.
A dot marks what needs a look, with its fix beside it: a gap to fill, a weekday that isn’t its date’s, words hard to read or too near the edge.
A date, a place or a phone number you didn’t give is never invented. Where the design can’t do without one, it leaves a gap in square brackets.
where.title: Where your design goes.
where.why: No {name} server keeps your design in a form it can read. What changes is the AI that answers, and you choose it.
where.cards: Your design is one file in your browser, encrypted. Nothing we can read reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
Your request and what you attach go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
Picking a take, moving a part or changing a colour happens on your device: nothing is sent, and no AI is asked.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. Without a sign-up, only the AI on this computer answers.
Its picture is made by an AI that draws, once you have one. Without one, the design keeps a frame for a photo of yours.
One page. Not yet: drawing by hand, grouping parts, turning one round, several pages, removing a picture’s background.
A design isn’t worked on together yet: one person finishes it at a time.
{name} can be wrong. Read the date and the place again before you print fifty.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
Invitations, posters, flyers, cards, menus, certificates and posts: anything to print, post or send as a picture, on one page.
Yes. Pick another take, then move, resize or delete any part, change its colours and type, and add words, a photo, a shape, an ornament or a QR code.
Yes: as a page to print or save as PDF, two A5s or four A6s to a sheet, or as a picture.
Can it use my colours and my logo?
Yes. With a design system set, the first take wears your colours and fonts, and your logo goes in its corner.
Does it work in my language?
Yes: its words are yours, right to left too, in type that has every letter of your language.
end.title: Try it with the studio’s post.
end.why: The request opens in {name} and is answered at once, or as soon as you choose an AI. Then give your own facts.
